CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess ongoing management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns today for a follow-up visit, reporting mixed results regarding his treatment plan. He indicates that while his sleep quality has remained stable, with an average of 8 hours per night, he still encounters difficulties with sleep onset. Mr. Smith states that the trazodone at 75 mg has been somewhat effective in minimizing nocturnal awakenings, but he continues to experience episodes of restlessness prior to sleep. He expresses frustration over these persistent issues, which he feels contribute to his overall emotional well-being.
In terms of fatigue, Mr. Smith notes a slight exacerbation, particularly during high-stress work periods. He describes feeling overwhelmed by project deadlines, which he believes has led to increased fatigue and occasional feelings of irritability. His headache frequency remains at three times per week, with an intensity of 5 out of 10. He has been using ibuprofen more frequently, approximately 2-3 times per week, to manage breakthrough headaches, which he feels have become slightly more intense.
Mr. Smith continues to engage in his holistic treatment approach, attending acupuncture sessions and practicing yoga. He reports that mindfulness techniques have been beneficial, but he recognizes the need for additional coping strategies to manage work-related stress. His anxiety levels remain stable, with no significant fluctuations reported since the last visit.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (increased usage noted) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (usage stable)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where the pressure from project deadlines has intensified. He maintains an active lifestyle, regularly attending yoga classes and practicing meditation. He abstains from alcohol and adheres to a plant-based diet, although he admits to occasional consumption of processed foods during stressful periods.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep initiation difficulties persist; anxiety remains manageable but noted to be slightly increased due to work stress; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency and intensity have increased; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Increased fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with noted fatigue.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Reinforce the importance of tapering lorazepam use as needed. Recommend scheduling additional therapy sessions to address work-related stress management techniques. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 75 mg; continue melatonin at 10 mg; explore alternative sleep hygiene strategies and consider a sleep study if sleep onset issues persist. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly. Due to increased ibuprofen usage, consider initiating topiramate for preventive therapy if headache frequency or intensity escalates further. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage ongoing physical activity and mindfulness practices. Discuss potential referral to a nutritionist to optimize dietary habits, especially during high-stress periods.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-06-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment efficacy, and consider further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
